statement: Let V(n) be the set of all sequences q = (q[0],...,q[n-1]) such that each q[i] is in {0,1,...,n-1} and for all 0 <= i < j < n we have q[i] != q[j], q[i] - q[j] != i - j, and q[i] - q[j] != j - i. The function returns a result r and r = |V(n)|. Thus r is the number of ways to place n non-attacking queens on an n x n board, row i having its queen in column q[i], with solutions that differ by any board symmetry counted separately unless they are the same sequence.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 9, where n is the integer value of the Std.I64 argument.
